question.text: Using put-call parity, if a call option is priced at Rs. 5, the spot price is Rs. 100, the present value of the strike is Rs. 97, what should the put option price be?

explanation.text: The Logic: Put-call parity (European options) states C + PV(X) = P + S, so P = C + PV(X) - S = 5 + 97 - 100 = Rs. 2. The Trap: Rs. 8 arises if a candidate computes C + S - PV(K), i.e. adds the spot instead of subtracting it. Rs. 3 results from using the strike itself instead of its present value PV(K). Note: Put-call parity holds exactly for European options; for American options early-exercise features can cause observed prices to deviate from the parity relation.
